title: Khachapuri
subtitle: Georgian cheese-filled bread with egg yolk
excerpt: Georgia's iconic bread: an oval boat of leavened dough filled with a creamy mixture of suluguni and feta, baked until the crust is golden and the filling is bubbling, then finished with a raw egg yolk and butter stirred in at the table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Khachapuri (from the Georgian words khacho, meaning cheese curds, and puri, bread) is the national dish of Georgia and exists in several regional forms across the Caucasus. The Adjaruli version (from the Adjara region on the Black Sea coast) is the most theatrical: an oval boat of bread filled with molten cheese, finished with an egg yolk and butter stirred in at the table by the diner. Other regional versions include the Imeruli (round, filled bread like a Georgian quesadilla), the Megruli (round with cheese on top), and the Penovani (layered, folded pastry). Suluguni, the traditional Georgian cheese, is a salty, slightly tangy, semi-hard cheese that melts well; a mixture of feta and mozzarella approximates its character outside Georgia.

content.text: Shape the boats carefully so the sides are high enough to contain the filling without spillage. The filling should be quite wet; mix the cheeses with a little egg to bind them and some cream or milk to give a melting texture. The raw egg yolk goes in right at the end, removed from the oven, and is stirred into the molten cheese at the table.

to stir in at the table

content.text: Make the dough: mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt. Add the warm milk and oil and mix to a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled. Meanwhile, mix the filling: combine feta, mozzarella, 2 beaten eggs, and 2 tablespoons of milk.

Heat the oven to 230°C / fan 210°C / gas 8 with a baking tray inside. Divide the dough into 4. Roll each piece into an oval about 25 x 15 cm. Place on a piece of baking paper. Fill the centre with the cheese mixture, leaving a 3 cm border. Roll and twist the long edges upwards to form a boat shape, pinching the ends.

Slide the breads onto the hot baking tray. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling. Remove from the oven. Make a well in the centre of each and drop in an egg yolk. Return to the oven for 1 minute only: the yolk should be barely set. Bring to the table with butter; stir the yolk and butter into the molten cheese before eating.
